offense_class: Misdemeanor (Levels I-V based on grossly aggravating/aggravating/mitigating factors); Felony (Habitual DWI)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on any highway, street, or public vehicular area
While under the influence of an impairing substance
OR with BAC of 0.08% or more (0.04% CDL holders; 0.00% under age 21 on limited permit)
mandatory_minimum: Level I: 30 days jail (active); Aggravated Level 1: 12 months active minimum
enhancements: Grossly aggravating factors: prior DWI within 7 years, serious injury accident, child passenger, driving on revoked license for DWI
Aggravated Level 1: two or more grossly aggravating factors — mandatory 12 months minimum active
Child under 18 in vehicle: grossly aggravating factor
notes: NC uses a tiered sentencing structure (Levels 1-5 plus Aggravated Level 1) based on aggravating and mitigating factors under § 20-179. Habitual DWI is a Class F felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (Level II-V typically for first offense with no aggravating factors)
elements: First DWI within 7-year look-back for sentencing purposes
Drove a vehicle on highway, street, or public vehicular area
While under influence or with BAC 0.08%+
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours jail (Level V minimum); 7 days (Level III)
enhancements: BAC 0.15% or higher: mandatory continuous alcohol monitoring (CAM)
Child passenger: grossly aggravating factor — elevates to Level I or Aggravated Level 1
notes: Most first offenses without aggravating factors are sentenced at Level V or IV. Ignition interlock required on restoration.

statute_title: Impaired Driving — Repeat Offense / Habitual DWI
offense_class: Misdemeanor (2nd within 7 years: Level I); Felony (Habitual DWI: Class F)
penalty_max: 12 months (Level I misdemeanor); 41 months (Class F felony Habitual DWI)
elements: Defendant has 3 or more prior DWI convictions within 10 years (Habitual DWI)
OR prior DWI within 7 years (grossly aggravating factor for Level I sentencing)
Drove while impaired as defined under § 20-138.1
mandatory_minimum: Level I: 30 days active minimum; Habitual DWI: 12 months active minimum
enhancements: Habitual DWI (Class F felony): mandatory 12 months active no suspension
Vehicle forfeiture possible on Habitual DWI
Permanent license revocation after Habitual DWI conviction
notes: 4th DWI within 10 years = Habitual DWI (Class F felony) under § 20-138.5. Permanent revocation possible.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (same tiers as alcohol DWI); Felony (Habitual DWI)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
With any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance in their blood or urine
OR while impaired by any impairing substance including prescription or OTC drugs
enhancements: Schedule I substance per se: no impairment proof required
Drug paraphernalia in vehicle: additional charge under § 90-113.22
notes: Per se provision under § 20-138.1(a)(3): any Schedule I substance in blood/urine = per se DWI. Covers marijuana metabolites.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 1 Misdemeanor (reckless endangering property)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a highway or public vehicular area
In a careless and heedless manner in willful or wanton disregard for the rights or safety of others
OR in a manner so as to endanger or be likely to endanger any person or property
enhancements: Resulting injury or death: felony death by vehicle or serious injury by vehicle charges
notes: 4 DMV points. Two types: willful/wanton disregard (§ 20-140(a)) and endangerment (§ 20-140(b)).

statute_title: Duty to Stop in Event of Accident — Hit and Run
offense_class: Class F Felony (death or serious injury); Class H Felony (injury); Class 1 Misdemeanor (property only)
penalty_max: 41 months (Class F); 25 months (Class H); 120 days (Class 1 misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was driving a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in death, injury, or property damage
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene, give information, or render aid
enhancements: DUI concurrent: aggravated sentence
Death resulting: Class F felony
Serious injury: Class H felony
notes: Under § 20-166, driver must stop, remain, give information, and render aid. Property damage only is Class 1 misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony (impaired driving); Class E Felony (reckless); Class F Felony (other moving violation)
penalty_max: 204 months (Class D); 88 months (Class E); 41 months (Class F)
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
While violating N.C.G.S. § 20-138.1 (impaired driving) or other specified traffic law
Violation was a proximate cause of death
enhancements: DWI as predicate: Class D felony with enhanced punishment
Multiple deaths: consecutive sentences
notes: Aggravated felony death by vehicle under § 20-141.4(a1) applies when defendant has prior DWI within 7 years.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
While committing a moving traffic violation other than impaired driving
enhancements: Elevation to felony if defendant has prior DWI
notes: Misdemeanor death by vehicle under § 20-141.4(a2). Moving violation as predicate.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 1 Misdemeanor or Class I Felony (revoked for DWI)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on any street or highway
While defendant's license was revoked, suspended, or cancelled
Defendant had knowledge of the revocation or suspension
enhancements: License revoked for DWI: Class 1 misdemeanor or Class I felony depending on circumstances
Impaired driving while revoked for DWI: vehicle forfeiture possible
notes: If license was revoked because of an impaired driving offense, enhanced penalties apply under § 20-28(a1).

offense_class: Class H Felony; Class F Felony (if aggravating factors present)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a street, highway, or public vehicular area
While fleeing or attempting to elude a law enforcement officer
After the officer gave a visible or audible signal to stop
enhancements: Endangering others or exceeding speed by 15+ mph: Class F felony
Death or serious injury: additional charges
Two or more aggravating factors: Class E felony
notes: Class F felony when two or more aggravating factors (reckless driving, speed 15+ mph over limit, endangering persons). Class H felony baseline.

statute_title: Open Container of Alcoholic Beverage in Passenger Area
offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (driver); Class 3 Misdemeanor (passenger)
elements: Defendant consumed alcohol or had in the passenger area an open container of alcohol
While driving a motor vehicle on a highway or public vehicular area
Container had been opened or had broken seal
notes: Passengers also subject to charge. Vehicles for hire and recreational vehicles may have exceptions.

statute_title: Refusal of Chemical Analysis — Implied Consent
offense_class: Administrative (license revocation); civil penalty
penalty_max: 1-year civil license revocation (1st refusal); permanent revocation (4th+)
elements: Defendant was lawfully arrested for impaired driving
Law enforcement officer informed defendant of implied consent rights
Defendant willfully refused to submit to chemical analysis
enhancements: 2nd refusal within 7 years: 4-year revocation
3rd or subsequent refusal: permanent revocation
notes: Refusal admissible at trial. NC requires Willful refusal — inadvertent or medical inability is not a refusal.

offense_class: Class I Felony (Schedule I-II); Class 1 Misdemeanor (Schedule III-VI under threshold)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance was listed on North Carolina's controlled substance schedules
Defendant had actual or constructive possession
enhancements: Near school, childcare center, or public park: Class E felony enhancement
Large quantity: trafficking threshold under § 90-95(h)
Prior drug felony: elevated class
notes: Marijuana possession of 0.5 oz or less is Class 3 misdemeanor. Over 0.5 oz: Class 1 misdemeanor. Over 1.5 oz: Class I felony.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (0.5 oz or less); Class 1 Misdemeanor (0.5-1.5 oz); Class I Felony (over 1.5 oz)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Amount determined classification
Possession was knowing
enhancements: Over 10 lbs: marijuana trafficking — Class H or higher felony with mandatory minimums
Near school or park: Class E felony enhancement
notes: Marijuana remains a controlled substance in NC (Schedule VI). No medical or recreational marijuana program as of 2026.

offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine (Schedule II)
Amount was below 28g trafficking threshold
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 28g or more: cocaine trafficking — Class G felony, mandatory 35 months minimum
Near school: Class E felony enhancement
notes: Cocaine trafficking under § 90-95(h)(3): 28g-200g = Class G (35 mo. min.); 200g-400g = Class F (70 mo. min.); 400g+ = Class D (175 mo. min.).

offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine (Schedule II)
Amount below 28g trafficking threshold
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 28g or more: meth trafficking — Class F felony, mandatory 70 months minimum
200g+ meth: Class D felony mandatory 175 months
notes: Meth trafficking thresholds: 28g-200g = Class F; 200g-400g = Class E; 400g+ = Class C under § 90-95(h)(3b).

offense_class: Class I Felony (Schedule I or II opiate)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed an opioid or opiate controlled substance
No valid prescription or prescription was fraudulently obtained
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 4g or more opium/heroin: trafficking — Class F mandatory 70 months
14g+ opium: Class E mandatory 90 months
28g+: Class D mandatory 175 months
notes: Heroin/opium trafficking under § 90-95(h)(4). Fentanyl treated as Schedule II. Distribution causing death may support murder.

statute_title: Possession of Prescription Drug Without Valid Prescription
offense_class: Class I Felony (Schedule II-III); Class 1 Misdemeanor (Schedule IV-VI)
elements: Defendant possessed a prescription controlled substance
Defendant lacked a valid, current prescription
Substance was on NC controlled substance schedule
enhancements: Doctor shopping or forged prescription: prescription fraud charge under § 90-108
notes: NC Controlled Substance Reporting System (CSRS) data used as evidence.

offense_class: Class G, F, E, D, or C Felony depending on substance and quantity
penalty_min: 35 months (cocaine 28g+, Class G); 70 months (cocaine 200g+, Class F)
elements: Defendant sold, manufactured, delivered, transported, or possessed with intent to sell or deliver a controlled substance
OR possessed any amount of a controlled substance in the trafficking quantity
Quantity met or exceeded the statutory trafficking threshold for the specific substance
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory minimum active sentence varies by substance and quantity; no probation permitted on mandatory term
enhancements: Prior drug trafficking conviction: enhanced mandatory minimum
Conspiracy to traffic: same penalties as completed trafficking
Leadership or organizer role: enhanced sentencing
notes: Trafficking quantities and classes vary by substance under § 90-95(h)(1)-(4). Mandatory active sentences; probation not available.

statute_title: Sale or Delivery of Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class G Felony (Schedule I-II); Class H Felony (Schedule III-IV); Class I Felony (Schedule V-VI)
penalty_max: 47 months (Class G); 39 months (Class H); 24 months (Class I)
elements: Defendant sold or delivered a controlled substance
Substance was on the controlled substance schedule
Defendant acted knowingly and intentionally
enhancements: Sale within 1,000 feet of school: two-class enhancement (e.g., Class G becomes Class E)
Sale to minor: enhanced penalty
Sale to pregnant woman: enhanced penalty
notes: School enhancement under § 90-95(e)(8) elevates offense two felony classes.

offense_class: Class H Felony (most drugs); Class D Felony (methamphetamine using precursors)
elements: Defendant manufactured, produced, or processed a controlled substance
Substance was on the controlled substance schedule
Acts were knowing and intentional
enhancements: Meth manufacturing using precursors: elevated to Class D felony under § 90-95(b1)
Children present at meth lab: child endangerment charges
Trafficking quantity: trafficking charges
notes: Manufacturing meth with precursor chemicals triggers Class D felony elevation under § 90-95(b1).

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia

Defendant intended to use the paraphernalia to plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, process, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale, or otherwise introduce a controlled substance into the human body
enhancements: Sale of paraphernalia to minor: Class I felony under § 90-113.22A
notes: Intent element is critical. Mere possession of an item without drug residue or proximity to drugs may be contested.

statute_title: Fraudulent Prescription / Obtaining a Controlled Substance by Fraud
offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant obtained or attempted to obtain a controlled substance by forgery, fraud, or deception
OR defendant used a forged or altered prescription
OR defendant used a false name or address with a practitioner
enhancements: Healthcare provider committing fraud: license revocation
Multiple fraudulent prescriptions: charges may stack
notes: NC Controlled Substance Reporting System (CSRS) tracks prescription patterns. Doctor-shopping prosecuted under § 90-108(a)(10).

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Sell or Deliver
offense_class: Class G Felony (Schedule I-II); Class H Felony (Schedule III-IV); Class I Felony (Schedule V-VI)
penalty_max: 47 months (Class G); 39 months (Class H); 24 months (Class I)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to sell or deliver
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, currency, or other evidence
enhancements: Near school or childcare center: two-class felony enhancement
With firearm: additional weapons charges
Trafficking quantity: trafficking charges
notes: Intent proven circumstantially. Quantity alone, without other indicators, generally insufficient for intent charge.

offense_class: Class A Felony
penalty_max: Death penalty or life without parole
elements: Defendant killed another human being
With malice, premeditation, and deliberation
OR by means of poison, lying in wait, imprisonment, starving, or torture
OR in the perpetration or attempted perpetration of a specified felony (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole (mandatory for Class A felony)
enhancements: Aggravating circumstances: death penalty eligible
Law enforcement officer victim: death penalty eligible aggravating circumstance
Especially heinous, atrocious, or cruel: aggravating circumstance
notes: NC has the death penalty. Felony murder covers killings during arson, rape, robbery, kidnapping, burglary, and other enumerated felonies.

offense_class: Class B1 Felony (malice without premeditation); Class B2 Felony (inherently dangerous act with malice)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class B2: 393 months+
elements: Defendant killed another human being
With malice
But without premeditation and deliberation
OR committed an act inherently dangerous to human life in wanton disregard of consequences
enhancements: Defendant had prior murder conviction: enhanced sentence
Drug distribution causing death: second-degree murder possible
notes: Class B1 felony — malice without premeditation. Class B2 — inherently dangerous act with reckless disregard.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant killed another human being
With malice but in the heat of passion
Upon adequate provocation that would cause a reasonable person to lose self-control
No cooling-off period had elapsed
notes: Heat-of-passion defense reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter (Class D felony). Imperfect self-defense may also result in voluntary manslaughter.

offense_class: Class F Felony
elements: Defendant killed another human being
Without malice or intent to kill
During commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony
OR during a lawful act performed in a culpably negligent manner
notes: Culpable negligence — greater than ordinary negligence. Vehicular deaths also charged under § 20-141.4.

statute_title: Assault with a Deadly Weapon Inflicting Serious Injury / Assault Inflicting Serious Bodily Injury
offense_class: Class C Felony (deadly weapon + intent to kill + serious injury); Class E Felony (serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
With a deadly weapon with intent to kill
Inflicting serious injury (Class C felony)
OR inflicted serious bodily injury without deadly weapon (Class E felony)
enhancements: Law enforcement officer victim: Class F felony (assault on officer) or higher
Strangulation: Class H felony under § 14-32.4(b)
Domestic violence context: additional charges
notes: Multiple assault statutes in NC. § 14-32 covers assault with deadly weapon. § 14-32.4 covers assault inflicting serious bodily injury.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (basic); Class A1 Misdemeanor (certain victims)
elements: Defendant committed a simple assault on another person
Either by an overt act creating reasonable apprehension of immediate bodily harm
OR by an actual physical act constituting battery
enhancements: Victim is female and defendant is male: Class A1 misdemeanor under § 14-33(c)(2)
Victim is child under 12: Class A1 misdemeanor
Victim is officer, teacher, healthcare worker: Class A1 misdemeanor
Domestic relationship: Class A1 misdemeanor
notes: NC combines assault and battery into one offense. Simple assault/battery is Class 2; assault on a female or child is Class A1.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (basic); Class A1 Misdemeanor (certain circumstances)
elements: Defendant intentionally made offensive, harmful, or provoking physical contact with another person
Without consent of the other person
enhancements: Serious bodily injury inflicted: Class E or C felony depending on circumstances
Domestic relationship: Class A1 misdemeanor
notes: NC treats assault and battery as the same offense under § 14-33. Battery requires physical contact; assault may be apprehension only.

offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
And inflicted serious bodily injury
Serious bodily injury means injury creating substantial risk of death or causing permanent disfigurement or protracted loss or impairment of function
enhancements: Deadly weapon used: potential elevation to Class C felony
Strangulation: Class H felony under § 14-32.4(b)
Victim is officer: Class F felony
notes: Strangulation causing physical injury separately classified as Class H felony under § 14-32.4(b).

offense_class: Class G Felony
elements: Defendant took property from another person or their presence
By use of force or intimidation
Without consent and with intent to permanently deprive
enhancements: Armed robbery: elevated to Class D felony under § 14-87
notes: Common law robbery under § 14-87.1 is Class G felony. Armed robbery (dangerous weapon) is Class D felony under § 14-87.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant took property from another person or their presence
By use of or threatened use of a firearm or other dangerous weapon
Victim was endangered or threatened
Defendant intended to permanently deprive the victim of the property
enhancements: Serious injury inflicted: enhanced sentence
Multiple victims: consecutive sentences
notes: Class D felony with presumptive active sentence. Dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and any object capable of threatening life.

offense_class: Class C Felony (1st degree — victim not released in safe place, or serious injury/sexual assault); Class E Felony (2nd degree)
elements: Defendant unlawfully confined, restrained, or removed from one place to another any person under 16, or any person by force, threat, or deception
Without consent of the victim (or parent/guardian if minor)
For purpose of holding for ransom, facilitating felony, doing serious harm, or terrorizing victim
enhancements: Victim not released in a safe place: 1st degree (Class C)
Sexual assault or serious injury during kidnapping: 1st degree
Ransom demand: Class C
notes: 1st degree (Class C) vs. 2nd degree (Class E) based on whether victim was released safely and whether sexual assault or serious injury occurred.

offense_class: Class D Felony (1st degree — occupied dwelling); Class G Felony (2nd degree — unoccupied or other structure)
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned a dwelling house or other structure
Dwelling was occupied by any person (1st degree)
OR structure was not an occupied dwelling (2nd degree)
enhancements: Person present and in danger: 1st degree
Insurance fraud motive: insurance fraud charges added
Burning school, government building: enhanced under § 14-49 et seq.
notes: Common law arson definitions used. Burning of non-dwelling structures covered under § 14-62 et seq.

statute_title: Attempted First or Second Degree Murder
offense_class: Class B1 Felony (attempted 1st degree murder); Class C Felony (attempted 2nd degree murder)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class C: 231 months
elements: Defendant took a substantial step toward committing murder
With the specific intent to kill
Act was beyond mere preparation
enhancements: Firearm used: enhanced sentencing
Victim is law enforcement: aggravating factor
notes: NC penalizes attempt at one class below the completed offense under § 14-2.5. Attempted 1st degree murder is Class B1 (same as 2nd degree murder).

offense_class: Class E Felony (deadly weapon + serious injury); Class A1 Misdemeanor (deadly weapon without serious injury)
penalty_max: 88 months (Class E felony); 150 days (Class A1 misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
With a deadly weapon
Inflicting serious injury (felony) OR not inflicting serious injury (misdemeanor)
enhancements: With intent to kill and serious injury: Class C felony
Law enforcement victim: enhanced charge
notes: Deadly weapon with serious injury = Class E. Deadly weapon + intent to kill + serious injury = Class C under § 14-32(a).

offense_class: Class I Felony ($1,000+); Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
Without consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Value $100,000+: Class C felony under § 14-72(b)(5)
From person or from fire or natural disaster victim: Class H felony
Theft of firearm: Class H felony regardless of value
notes: Felony larceny threshold is $1,000. Larceny from the person (Class H) does not require force — that would be robbery.

offense_class: Class I Felony ($1,000+); Class H Felony (larceny from person, firearm, or other specified circumstances)
elements: Defendant took and carried away personal property of another
Without consent
Property value was $1,000 or more OR circumstances elevated to felony
Intent to permanently deprive
enhancements: Theft from person: Class H
Theft of firearm: Class H
Value $100,000+: Class C
notes: NC uses 'larceny' not 'theft.' Felony threshold is $1,000.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant took and carried away personal property of another
Without consent and with intent to permanently deprive
Property value was under $1,000
enhancements: Prior larceny convictions: potential elevation to felony for repeat offenders under § 14-72(b)(3)
notes: Third conviction for misdemeanor larceny is a Class I felony under § 14-72(b)(3).

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class 2 Misdemeanor (2nd offense); Class 1 Misdemeanor (3rd offense); Class I Felony (4th+ or value over $2,000)
elements: Defendant concealed merchandise on the premises of a retail merchant
With intent to take possession of the merchandise without paying the merchant's stated price
Merchandise was not yet purchased
enhancements: 4th or subsequent offense: Class I felony
Value over $2,000: Class I felony regardless of prior record
Organized retail theft: Class H felony under § 14-72.12
notes: Escalating classification for repeat offenders. Merchant detention privilege under § 14-72.1(c).

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house or sleeping apartment
Dwelling was actually occupied at the time
In the nighttime
With intent to commit a felony or larceny therein
enhancements: Person present and in danger: enhanced sentence
Armed during burglary: additional weapons charges
notes: 1st degree burglary (Class D) requires occupied dwelling and nighttime. 2nd degree (Class G) under § 14-51 covers daytime or unoccupied dwelling.

offense_class: Class D Felony (1st degree, occupied nighttime); Class G Felony (2nd degree)
elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house
With intent to commit a felony or larceny therein
1st degree: dwelling occupied and crime committed in nighttime
enhancements: Victim present: significant sentencing factor
Prior burglary: enhanced sentence
notes: North Carolina common law requirements for breaking and entering apply. Uninvited entry through open door may still constitute breaking.

offense_class: Class H Felony (felonious intent); Class 1 Misdemeanor (without felonious intent)
elements: Defendant broke or entered a building
With intent to commit any felony or larceny therein
enhancements: Person present: sentencing enhancement
Weapon possessed: additional charges
notes: Broader than common law burglary — covers non-dwelling structures, daytime, and does not require both breaking and entering.

offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant received, transferred, possessed, concealed, or was found operating a motor vehicle
Knowing the motor vehicle was stolen
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Carjacking: robbery or armed robbery charges
Vehicle used in commission of crime: additional charges
notes: Vehicle larceny also prosecuted under general larceny statute § 14-72. Motor vehicle theft is Class I felony.

offense_class: Class I Felony (value $1,000+); Class 1 Misdemeanor (value under $1,000)
elements: Defendant received or possessed stolen goods
Defendant knew or had reasonable grounds to believe the goods were stolen
Intent to dishonestly retain the goods
enhancements: Motor vehicle: enhanced charges under § 20-106
Value over $100,000: Class C felony
notes: Same felony threshold as larceny: $1,000. Knowledge element — reasonable grounds to believe is an objective standard.

statute_title: Willful and Wanton Injury to Real Property
offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (value under $200); Class I Felony (value $200+) under § 14-127
elements: Defendant willfully and wantonly damaged or destroyed real property of another
Without authority or justification
Act was intentional
enhancements: Religious or educational institution: enhanced under § 14-49.1
Hate crime motivation: enhanced under § 14-3(c)
notes: Also see § 14-159.4 (injury to personal property). Damage to railroad property under § 14-138. Hate crime enhancement doubles maximum under § 14-3(c).

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (1st degree); Class 3 Misdemeanor (2nd degree)
elements: Defendant entered or remained on the premises of another person
Without authorization after being notified not to enter or remain
OR entered an enclosed or posted property (1st degree: with intent to damage property or after notice; 2nd degree: without notice but enclosed/posted)
enhancements: Critical infrastructure trespass: Class I felony under § 14-159.12(b)
Operating chemical facility: enhanced felony
notes: 1st degree (Class 2) requires notice or intent to damage. 2nd degree (Class 3) covers trespass on enclosed/posted property without notice.

statute_title: Willful Injury to Real or Personal Property
offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $200 real property); Class I Felony (over $200); Class 2 Misdemeanor (personal property under $200)
elements: Defendant willfully and wantonly injured, damaged, or destroyed property of another
notes: NC uses 'willful injury to property' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Classification depends on value and type of property.

statute_title: Domestic Violence — Assault on a Female / Domestic Violence Assault
offense_class: Class A1 Misdemeanor; Felony if serious injury
penalty_max: 150 days (Class A1); up to 88 months (Class E felony with serious injury)
elements: Defendant committed an assault on a current or former intimate partner, household member, or person with whom they have a child
OR defendant committed assault on a female if defendant is male (§ 14-33(c)(2))
Act was intentional
enhancements: Prior conviction of assault on female or crime of domestic violence: Class A1 misdemeanor at minimum
Strangulation: Class H felony under § 14-32.4(b)
Serious injury: escalated felony class
notes: Domestic violence covered under Chapter 50B civil protective orders and criminal assault statutes. Strangulation is separately Class H felony.

statute_title: Assault on a Female / Domestic Battery
offense_class: Class A1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant is male
Defendant assaulted a female
Acts were intentional
enhancements: Serious bodily injury: Class E felony under § 14-32.4
Strangulation: Class H felony under § 14-32.4(b)
notes: Assault on a female under § 14-33(c)(2) requires defendant to be male and victim female. Gender-neutral serious assault under § 14-32.4.

statute_title: Child Abuse / Contributing to the Delinquency of a Minor
offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (contributing); Class A1 Misdemeanor (child abuse by parent); Class C or D Felony (serious injury or sexual abuse)
elements: Defendant is a parent, legal guardian, or caretaker of a juvenile under 16
Defendant inflicted or allowed infliction of physical injury upon the juvenile
OR defendant committed, permitted, or encouraged acts constituting child abuse
enhancements: Serious physical injury: Class D felony
Sexual abuse of child under 13: Class C felony with mandatory registration
notes: Child abuse with serious injury is Class D felony under § 14-318.4(a3). Sexual abuse is Class C felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony (serious physical injury); Class C Felony (sexual abuse, child under 13)
elements: Defendant is a parent, legal guardian, or caretaker of a child under 16
Defendant inflicted or allowed infliction of serious physical injury upon the child
OR committed sexual abuse upon a child under 13
enhancements: Pattern of abuse: aggravating factor
Death resulting: murder charges
notes: Felony child abuse under § 14-318.4 for parents and caretakers. Strangers may be charged under assault statutes.

statute_title: Violation of Domestic Violence Protective Order
offense_class: Class A1 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class H Felony (2nd+ violation or violation with assault)
elements: A valid domestic violence protective order under Chapter 50B had been issued
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant violated the specific terms of the order
enhancements: 2nd or subsequent violation: Class H felony
Assault during violation: Class H felony on 1st offense
notes: Violations involving assault are Class H felony on first offense. Federal firearm prohibition applies under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(8).

offense_class: Class A1 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class F Felony (2nd+ offense or violation of protective order)
elements: Defendant followed, was in the presence of, or contacted another person on at least two occasions
Without consent
Causing that person to reasonably fear for their safety, a family member's safety, or to suffer substantial emotional distress
Defendant knew or should have known the conduct would cause fear or distress
enhancements: 2nd conviction or violation of protective order: Class F felony
Use of electronic means: cyberstalking enhancement
notes: Cyberstalking under § 14-196.3 separately covers electronic harassment. Two separate incidents required.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant made telephone calls or electronic communications to another person
With intent to harass, annoy, or embarrass
OR used repeated calls with no purpose of communication
enhancements: Cyberstalking: elevated charges under § 14-196.3
Threatening communications: terroristic threat charges
notes: Cyberstalking under § 14-196.3 covers electronic harassment intended to cause fear or emotional distress.

statute_title: Domestic Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation of Disabled or Elder Adult
offense_class: Class H Felony (abuse/neglect); Class I Felony (exploitation)
elements: Defendant was a caregiver or person responsible for a disabled or elder adult (65+)
Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited the person in their care
OR financially exploited the elder or disabled adult
enhancements: Serious physical injury: Class G or higher felony
Death resulting: murder or manslaughter charges
notes: Financial exploitation separately addressed under § 14-32.3(b). Adult Protective Services mandatory reporting required.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class H Felony (2nd+ offense or concealed handgun without permit)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon off their own premises
Without a valid concealed carry permit
With knowledge of possession
enhancements: 2nd offense: Class H felony
Carrying on school premises: Class I felony under § 14-269.2
Armed during commission of felony: additional charges
notes: NC has shall-issue CHP. Carrying without permit is Class 2 misdemeanor first offense. School property carrying is Class I felony.

offense_class: Class G Felony
elements: Defendant was convicted of a felony
Defendant purchased, owned, possessed, or had in custody, care, or control a firearm
With knowledge of possession
enhancements: Use of firearm in commission of a crime: additional charges
Federal concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1)
Prior violent felony: enhanced sentence
notes: Class G felony. Rights restoration possible through pardon or expungement of underlying felony.

statute_title: Carrying Concealed Handgun Without Valid Permit
offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class H Felony (2nd+ offense)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed handgun off their own premises
Without a valid concealed handgun permit
enhancements: 2nd offense: elevated to Class H felony
notes: Handgun carry without permit escalates to Class H felony on 2nd offense. CHP available to qualifying residents.

statute_title: Discharging a Barreled Weapon Into Occupied Property
offense_class: Class D Felony (into occupied property); Class E Felony (into property not reasonably believed occupied)
elements: Defendant willfully or wantonly discharged a firearm, barreled weapon, or other deadly weapon
Into any building, structure, or vehicle
When the property was occupied or defendant had reasonable cause to believe it was occupied
enhancements: Person injured or killed: additional charges
School or government building: enhanced sentence
notes: Class D felony for discharge into occupied property. Reckless discharge otherwise charged under assault statutes.

statute_title: Possession of Machine Gun or Sawed-Off Shotgun
offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant possessed, sold, or transferred a machine gun, sawed-off shotgun, or sawed-off rifle
Without NFA registration
With knowledge of the nature of the weapon
enhancements: Use in commission of a crime: additional charges
Federal NFA violation: concurrent federal charges
notes: NFA-registered weapons are legal with proper registration. State crime for unregistered NFA items.

offense_class: Class G Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, possessed, or used identifying information of another person
Without that person's consent
With intent to fraudulently represent themselves as that person
For any unlawful purpose
enhancements: More than 3 victims: Class F felony
Elder victim (65+): enhanced penalty
Use of internet or electronic means: additional charges
notes: Multiple victims enhancement under § 14-113.20A. Aggravated identity theft (3+ victims or financial institution) is Class F felony.

offense_class: Class H Felony (value under $100,000); Class C Felony (value $100,000+)
elements: Defendant was entrusted with or had access to property belonging to another
Defendant fraudulently appropriated the property
To defendant's own use or the use of another person not entitled to the property
With intent to defraud the owner
enhancements: Public official embezzlement: enhanced penalties
Value $100,000+: Class C felony
notes: Embezzlement by public official may be a Class F felony under § 14-92. Financial institution embezzlement carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class I Felony
elements: Defendant forged or counterfeited an instrument
With intent to defraud
Instrument could affect legal rights (checks, deeds, contracts, etc.)
enhancements: Public official's signature forged: Class H felony
Multiple forgeries: charges may stack
notes: Uttering forged instrument separately charged under § 14-120. Both can be charged together.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (under $2,000); Class 1 Misdemeanor ($2,000-$9,999); Class I Felony ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant drew, made, or delivered a check, draft, or order
Defendant knew at time of delivery that funds were insufficient or no account existed
Payee was defrauded
enhancements: Amount aggregated over multiple bad checks: may reach felony threshold
notes: 10-day grace period after notice allows payment and avoids prosecution. Three-tier classification based on amount.

offense_class: Class H Felony (value under $100,000); Class C Felony (value $100,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly and designedly, by false pretense, obtained or attempted to obtain
From another person, property, money, valuable consideration, or other thing
With intent to cheat and defraud
The false pretense was the operating cause of the transfer
enhancements: Elder victim (65+): enhanced penalty
Internet or wire used: additional charges
Value $100,000+: Class C felony
notes: Common fraud vehicle in NC. Represents the historical false pretenses offense.

offense_class: Class G Felony (state); Federal felony
elements: Defendant used wire, radio, or television communications in interstate or foreign commerce
To execute a scheme to defraud
OR to obtain money or property by means of false pretenses or representations
enhancements: Financial institution victim: enhanced federal penalty
Large monetary loss: enhanced sentence
notes: Wire fraud primarily prosecuted federally. NC state fraud charges typically used for local transactions.

offense_class: Class H Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented false, incomplete, or misleading information to an insurer
In connection with an insurance claim, application, or transaction
With intent to defraud the insurer
enhancements: Healthcare insurance fraud: enhanced penalties under specific healthcare fraud statutes
Organized fraud ring: conspiracy charges
notes: NC Department of Insurance investigates insurance fraud. Workers' comp fraud separately addressed.

offense_class: Class H Felony (state)
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction involving proceeds of unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property was the proceeds of unlawful activity
With intent to promote or conceal the unlawful activity
enhancements: Federal parallel prosecution: 18 U.S.C. § 1956
Drug trafficking proceeds: enhanced
notes: Most money laundering cases prosecuted federally. NC Class H felony for state prosecutions.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant acted in such a manner as to be reasonably likely to provoke a violent response from another person
OR disturbed the peace by making a loud and raucous noise
OR disrupted the orderly conduct of a lawful meeting, gathering, or procession
notes: Disorderly conduct in a public place under § 14-132 (Class 2). Emergency management-related disorderly conduct under § 14-288.4.

statute_title: Resisting, Delaying, or Obstructing a Public Officer
offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant willfully and unlawfully resisted, delayed, or obstructed a public officer
Officer was discharging or attempting to discharge a duty of the officer's office
Defendant knew or had reasonable grounds to know the person was a public officer
enhancements: Assault on officer during resistance: Class F or higher felony
Injury to officer: Class E felony
notes: Misdemeanor for resistance alone. Assaulting an officer is separate and more serious charge under § 14-34.2.

offense_class: Class H Felony (obstruction of justice); Class 2 Misdemeanor (obstructing officer)
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impeded, or hindered an official proceeding or criminal investigation
Act was knowing and intentional
Act was not authorized or justified
enhancements: Evidence tampering: additional charges
Witness intimidation or retaliation: Class F or G felony under § 14-226
notes: Obstruction of justice is a common law offense in NC, codified as Class H felony. Witness intimidation separately classified.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (simple criminal contempt); more severe depending on conduct
penalty_max: 30 days imprisonment per occurrence (simple); 120 days (Class 1 misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful court order
OR engaged in conduct that disrupted, impaired, or obstructed the administration of justice
Conduct was directly or indirectly contrary to a specific order
enhancements: Repeated contempt: consecutive penalties
Domestic violence order violation: Class A1 misdemeanor or Class H felony
notes: Summary contempt may be imposed by judge without separate hearing for conduct in the courtroom.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant appeared in a public place
In an intoxicated condition
And was disruptive as indicated by boisterous and noisy conduct, threatening or fighting, or creating a hazard
notes: Simple intoxication in public is not a crime in NC — disruptive element required. Protective custody available as alternative.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant remained in a public place
For the purpose of engaging in unlawful activity or soliciting
After being asked to move along by an officer
notes: NC loitering statutes must be applied carefully to avoid First Amendment concerns. Specific purpose element required.

offense_class: Class I Felony (felony underlying charge); Class 2 Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying charge)
elements: Defendant was released from custody pursuant to a written promise to appear
Defendant had notice of the appearance date
Defendant failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is violent felony: enhanced sentence
Bond forfeiture: civil consequences for surety
notes: Order for arrest issued upon FTA. Written promise to appear required for criminal FTA charge.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant made a statement or report to a law enforcement officer
Defendant knew the statement was false
Statement was made in connection with a criminal investigation
enhancements: Swatting: Class H felony or Class F felony if injury results
False report causing death: enhanced charges
notes: Separate from perjury or false swearing. Swatting addressed under § 14-225.1 as Class H felony, Class F if injury results.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant threatened to physically injure another person or their family members, household members, or property
The threat was communicated to that person
Defendant had the ability to carry out the threat
Recipient believed the defendant would carry out the threat
enhancements: Threat related to judicial proceedings: obstruction of justice
Bomb threat or weapon of mass destruction: Class H felony under § 14-277.1A
notes: Bomb threats or threats involving nuclear, biological, chemical, or radiological agents: Class H or Class F felony under § 14-277.1A.

offense_class: Depends on original underlying offense
penalty_max: Active sentence up to the original maximum
elements: Defendant was on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was willful or without lawful excuse
enhancements: New criminal offense: revocation plus new charges
Absconding: violation of condition warranting revocation
notes: NC JRA (2011) limits technical revocations to 90-day jail terms on first two technical violations. Active sentence only on third violation or new offense.

offense_class: Administrative — limited confinement
penalty_max: 90 days confinement (1st technical); 90 days (2nd); active sentence (3rd)
elements: Defendant was on probation
Defendant violated a non-criminal technical condition (failure to report, failure to pay fees, positive drug test)
notes: NC JRA 2011 limits technical revocations: 90 days for 1st and 2nd technical violations; active sentence only on 3rd or for absconding/new offense.

statute_title: Substantive Probation Violation — New Criminal Offense
offense_class: Probation revocation plus new criminal charges
elements: Defendant was on probation
Defendant committed a new criminal offense while on probation
New offense constitutes a violation of probation conditions
notes: New offense on probation triggers full revocation hearing. Court may impose active sentence up to original maximum.

offense_class: Administrative — return to prison
penalty_max: Return to custody; re-incarceration for balance of sentence
elements: Defendant was on post-release supervision or parole
Defendant violated conditions of supervision
Post-Release Supervision and Parole Commission determined violation warranted revocation
enhancements: New felony conviction while on supervision: mandatory revocation
notes: NC Post-Release Supervision Commission handles revocations. Structured sentencing affects parole eligibility.

offense_class: One class below target offense felony; Class 1 Misdemeanor (if target is misdemeanor)
penalty_max: One class below the completed target offense
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit an offense
Defendant was a party to the agreement
Each party had the intent to carry out the agreement
An overt act in furtherance not required in NC
enhancements: Drug trafficking conspiracy: same mandatory minimums as completed trafficking under § 90-95(h)
RICO-type conduct: potential enterprise liability
notes: NC conspiracy is one class below the target offense under § 14-2.4. No overt act required. Drug trafficking conspiracy treated same as completed trafficking.

statute_title: First Degree Rape / Second Degree Rape
offense_class: Class B1 Felony (1st degree); Class C Felony (2nd degree)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class C: 231 months
elements: Defendant engaged in vaginal intercourse with a victim
By force and against the will of the victim (2nd degree)
OR victim was under 13 and defendant is 12+ and at least 4 years older (1st degree)
OR defendant used or displayed a dangerous weapon, or aided by another person, or inflicted serious injury (1st degree)
enhancements: Victim under 13: mandatory sex offender registration for life
Prior sex offense: aggravated sentence
notes: NC overhauled sexual assault statutes effective December 1, 2023. New statutes use 'rape' for vaginal intercourse; sexual assault for other acts.

statute_title: First Degree Sexual Assault / Second Degree Sexual Assault
offense_class: Class B1 Felony (1st degree); Class C Felony (2nd degree)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class C: 231 months
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual act with another person
By force and against the will of the victim (2nd degree)
OR victim was under 13 and defendant is 12+ and at least 4 years older (1st degree)
Sexual act means oral or anal sex, or penetration by object
enhancements: Use of dangerous weapon: 1st degree classification
Multiple attackers: 1st degree
Victim under 13: mandatory lifetime registration
notes: 2023 NC statutory revision replaced 'sexual offense' with 'sexual assault' for clarity. Covers all sexual acts other than vaginal intercourse.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (1st offense); Class H Felony (in presence of minor under 16)
elements: Defendant willfully exposed the private parts of their person
In any public place in the presence of any person other than the defendant
In a lewd and lascivious manner
enhancements: Exposure in presence of minor under 16: Class H felony
On school premises: enhanced charges
notes: Exposure in presence of minor under 16 is automatically Class H felony with sex offender registration possible.

offense_class: Class B1 Felony (victim under 13, defendant 12+, 4 yrs older); Class C Felony (defendant 22+, victim 15 or younger); Class C Felony (defendant 18+, victim 13-15)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class C: 231 months
elements: Defendant engaged in vaginal intercourse with a person of a specific age
Defendant was the specified number of years older than the victim
Consent is not a defense
notes: NC has tiered statutory rape: § 14-27.23 (Class B1, victim under 13); § 14-27.24 (Class C, victim 13-15, defendant 18+); § 14-27.25 (defendant 22+). Close-in-age exemption: 4-6 years depending on section.

offense_class: Class C Felony (1st degree — production); Class E Felony (2nd degree — distribution/possession for distribution); Class H Felony (3rd degree — possession)
penalty_max: 231 months (Class C); 88 months (Class E); 39 months (Class H)
elements: Defendant used a minor to engage in sexual activity for a visual depiction
OR distributed, transported, exhibited, received, sold, purchased, or possessed visual depictions of minors in sexual activity
Minor was under 18
enhancements: Production: Class C felony
Distribution for profit: enhanced
Federal concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 2252
notes: Three-tier classification: production (Class C), distribution (Class E), possession (Class H) under § 14-190.13 et seq.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Class F Felony
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender under N.C.G.S. Chapter 14 Article 27A
Defendant failed to register, update registration, or comply with verification requirements
Defendant had actual knowledge of the registration requirement
enhancements: Prior registration violation: enhanced sentence
Absconding from jurisdiction: additional charges
notes: Sex offender registration under N.C.G.S. Chapter 14, Article 27A. Lifetime registration for certain offenses.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (prostitution/solicitation); Class G Felony (promoting/facilitating)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual activity for hire or solicited another person to engage in sexual activity for hire
Exchange of consideration was part of the transaction
enhancements: Minor victim: sex trafficking charges under § 14-43.11
Promoting or facilitating: Class G felony
Trafficking for sexual exploitation: Class B2 to E felony under § 14-43.11
notes: Human trafficking for sexual exploitation under § 14-43.11 is separate and carries Class B2-E felony charges.

offense_class: Class H Felony to Class B1 Felony depending on nature
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months; Class H: 39 months
elements: Defendant engaged in or facilitated a sexual act or exploitation through electronic or digital means
OR used the internet to solicit or entice a minor to engage in sexual activity
enhancements: Solicitation of minor: Class H felony under § 14-202.3
notes: Solicitation of a child by computer under § 14-202.3 is Class H or Class G felony depending on minor's age.

offense_class: Class A1 Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact with another person
By force and against the will of the other person
OR victim was mentally disabled or physically helpless
enhancements: Repeat offense: potential felony escalation
Victim under 13: more serious felony charge
notes: Sexual battery under § 14-27.33 is the lowest-level sexual offense in NC. Class A1 misdemeanor.

statute_title: First and Second Degree Sexual Exploitation / Statutory Sexual Offense
offense_class: Class B1 Felony (1st degree); Class C Felony (2nd degree)
penalty_max: Class B1: 484 months+; Class C: 231 months
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with a person
By force and against the will of the person (2nd degree)
OR victim was under 13 and defendant was 12+ and at least 4 years older (1st degree)
notes: NC 2023 reform renamed these offenses. Covers sexual acts (non-vaginal-intercourse) paralleling rape statutes.

offense_class: Affirmative defense — not an offense
elements: Defendant used force against another person
Defendant reasonably believed the force was necessary to prevent imminent death or serious bodily harm
Defendant was not the aggressor
Under Castle Doctrine (§ 14-51.2): presumption of reasonable fear when intruder enters home, motor vehicle, or workplace unlawfully
notes: NC has a Castle Doctrine (§ 14-51.2) with a rebuttable presumption of reasonable fear for home intrusions. No general Stand Your Ground statute (duty to retreat eliminated inside home). Outside home, duty to retreat still applies unless Castle Doctrine triggers.

offense_class: Varies
penalty_max: Varies by specific offense and class
elements: Elements specific to each offense as defined under the North Carolina General Statutes
notes: NC uses structured sentencing under the Fair Sentencing Act. Offense class and prior record level determine the sentencing range. Consult the specific N.C.G.S. section for elements, penalties, and prior record calculations.
